did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm presents reverence for the LORD and delight in His commandments as the foundation of a person’s happiness.
Did you know? The blessing of the person who reveres the LORD is also seen in his descendants: “His offspring will be mighty in the land,” and the generation of the upright will be blessed.
Did you know? The psalm links abundance in the home with generosity: the righteous person’s house contains wealth and riches, but his righteousness endures forever.
Did you know? Even in the darkness, light shines for the upright; the verse then lists their qualities: gracious, compassionate, and righteous.
Did you know? A good person shows kindness by giving and lending, but also by managing his affairs wisely and morally: “He conducts his affairs with justice.”
Did you know? The stability of the righteous is described in two ways: they will never be shaken, and their memory will endure.
Did you know? The righteous person is not afraid of bad news, because his heart is steadfast and secure in the LORD.
Did you know? The righteous person’s confidence is described as inner stability: his heart is secure, so he is not afraid until he sees his adversaries defeated.
Did you know? Giving to the poor is presented as an ongoing act with an honorable result: his righteousness endures forever, and his horn will be exalted with honor.
Did you know? The psalm’s conclusion contrasts the wicked person with the righteous: the wicked sees this, is angry, and grinds his teeth, but his desire comes to nothing.
